housing.summary: Berlin's rental market is highly competitive and tenant-protective. Most flats are unfurnished (often without kitchen/appliances) and let long-term. Newcomers typically need Schufa credit report, proof of income, and prior-landlord reference. Cold rent (Kaltmiete) excludes utilities; warm rent (Warmmiete) includes them. A rent cap (Mietspiegel) benchmarks legal rents. Expect strong demand in central districts (Mitte, Prenzlauer Berg, Kreuzberg, Charlottenburg).

banking.summary: Opening a current account (Girokonto) requires proof of address (registration/Anmeldung), passport/ID, and often the tax ID. Both traditional banks and app-based providers operate widely; many expats use digital banks for fast English-language onboarding. A local IBAN is essential for rent, salary and SEPA direct debits.
banking.required_docs: Passport or national ID, proof of address (Meldebescheinigung/Anmeldung), and tax identification number (Steueridentifikationsnummer); residence permit for non-EU nationals.
banking.banks_named: Deutsche Bank, Commerzbank, Sparkasse (Berliner Sparkasse), Postbank; digital: N26, Deutsche Kreditbank (DKB)

schools.summary: Berlin offers free public (state) schools taught in German, plus a large selection of bilingual, international, and private schools for expat families. International schools follow foreign or dual curricula and charge tuition; demand is high and waitlists common. School attendance is compulsory from age six.
schools.curricula: International Baccalaureate (IB), British (IGCSE/A-Level), American, French, German Abitur, and bilingual German-English state programs (Staatliche Europa-Schule Berlin).

legal_admin.summary: After arriving and securing housing, residents must register their address in person. Non-EU nationals additionally need a residence/work permit from the immigration office. Registration triggers issuance of the tax ID and is prerequisite for banking, health insurance and many services. Appointments are often required and can book out weeks ahead.
legal_admin.registration_step: Anmeldung (address registration) at a Bürgeramt within about two weeks of moving in, using passport and a landlord confirmation (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung).

tax_finance.summary: Germany assigns a lifelong tax ID automatically after address registration, mailed by the federal tax office. Employees are taxed via payroll (Lohnsteuer) with progressive rates plus solidarity surcharge and, if applicable, church tax. Tax class (Steuerklasse) affects withholding; annual returns are filed with the local tax office (Finanzamt).

transport.summary: Berlin has an extensive integrated public transport network covering U-Bahn (metro), S-Bahn (suburban rail), trams, buses and ferries across fare zones A/B/C. Tickets and monthly passes work across all modes. Cycling infrastructure is strong. A nationwide monthly ticket (Deutschlandticket) is also widely used.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences are valid; many non-EU licences must be exchanged (Umschreibung) within six months of residency, sometimes requiring theory/practical tests depending on the country of issue.
transport.healthcare_registration: Health insurance is mandatory. Register with a statutory health insurer (gesetzliche Krankenversicherung, e.g. TK, AOK, Barmer) or private insurance; employees are enrolled via their employer and choose a general practitioner (Hausarzt).
